title: Working on Pointer Pop, a match-3 mobile game about my real dog Pipi (a German Shorthaired Pointer). Solo dev from Paraguay.
author: Michilabsdev
selftext:
The game is free on Google Play if anyone wants to try it:

[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.michilabs.pointerpop](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.michilabs.pointerpop)

What was the problem?

With 300 levels and lots of obstacles (mud that grows, wind that drops leaves, cages, bubbles, items that must reach the bottom), players kept finding edge cases: boards with no possible moves that never reshuffled, items trapped forever inside a bubble, and goals that grew faster than you could clear them. Testing 300 levels by hand was impossible.



What was the solution?

1. A headless bot (GDScript) that plays every level with the exact same turn order as the real game, many runs per level, and reports: win %, stuck boards, reshuffles needed, infinite cascades and levels won too fast.

2. Every fix goes into the engine as a general rule, never as a per-level patch. For example:

   \- A 3-step reshuffle: normal shuffle, then a deep shuffle, then refill empty cells and shuffle again, so the board can never stay stuck.

   \- A trapped item is freed when its cage or bubble breaks, or by a match next to it.

   \- Wind can grow the leaf goal by at most 50% of the original amount. Before, every fallen leaf added +1 forever, and one stage could never be won.

3. After each change the bot runs again only on the affected levels and compares win rates before and after, so difficulty doesn't silently change.



What worked with AI coding agents?

\- The bot gives the agent a hard number to check against ("level 226: 100% wins, 0 stuck"), instead of "I think it works".

\- The game runs headless in the cloud, so the agent can import the project, run a compile check and the bot without opening the editor.

\- A short [CONTEXT.md](http://CONTEXT.md) in the repo with the rules of the project (what not to touch, how to test, backups) saves a lot of re-explaining between sessions.



Art was made with AI image tools from prompts; code and tests with Claude; sounds from Mixkit.



Happy to answer questions about the bot or the workflow.
